routes.description: Establish that Christianity offers humanity the brighter future by showing that its worldview grounds and sustains moral formation, rights-bearing institutions, social cooperation, meaning, and truth-seeking across generations.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if Christianity is shown to provide credible foundations and durable mechanisms for preserving human dignity, free institutions, social health, purposeful agency, and intellectual progress better than a society detached from those foundations.

motionBridge.description: Connect Christianity's claimed truth and formative effects to a comparatively brighter, freer, healthier, and more sustainable human future.

centralBridges.description: Show how Christian anthropology and historical formation ground human equality, rights, limited government, and protection of vulnerable people.
Show that Christian participation, motivation, community practices, and demographic continuity sustain social cooperation and liberal institutions over time.
Defend Christianity's coherence and evidential credibility while explaining how Christian commitments support reliable inquiry and scientific institutions.
Show that equal civil rights, practical cooperation, and appropriately bounded conscience protections can coexist within a Christian social framework.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain how Christian hope, purpose, and moral narrative motivate ordinary and disadvantaged people toward responsibility and social improvement.
Answer specific objections concerning suffering, agency, scripture, historical causation, and contested applications of religious liberty.

routes.description: Establish that humanism offers humanity the brighter future by showing that reason, shared human interests, and political secularism support moral responsibility, healthy societies, equal rights, truth-seeking, and pluralistic freedom without Christian foundations.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if humanism is shown to furnish inclusive moral and political commitments, credible methods of inquiry, and sustainable social arrangements while Christianity's asserted necessity, truth, and entitlement to public privilege remain unestablished.

motionBridge.description: Connect humanist moral autonomy, evidence-based inquiry, and state neutrality to a comparatively healthier, freer, and more inclusive human future.

centralBridges.description: Show that moral responsibility and shared commitments can rest on religiously neutral reasons accessible to Christians, non-Christians, and nonbelievers alike.
Show that healthy secular and non-Christian societies undermine claims that Christianity is necessary for decency, cooperation, institutional stability, or future flourishing.
Test the coherence, morality, and evidential support of Christian claims that would need to be credible before Christianity could serve as society's foundation.
Show that political secularism protects equal citizenship by withholding religious privilege and evaluating conscience claims without favoring their religious origin.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test whether Christianity deserves unique causal credit for rights, reform, science, and other achievements produced within historically Christian societies.
Test whether secularization causes harmful fertility decline and whether lower fertility or demographic change establishes Christianity's comparative necessity.

sections.title: Moral foundations, human dignity, and historical inheritance
sections.rationale: The motion requires comparing whether Christianity or humanism can ground moral responsibility and human worth, and whether the West's rights tradition depends on specifically Christian formation.

sections.title: Christian truth, evidence, suffering, and human agency
sections.rationale: Christianity's suitability as a future foundation depends partly on the coherence and evidential support of its claims about God, salvation, suffering, scripture, souls, and free agency.

sections.title: Social health, motivation, and generational sustainability
sections.rationale: Claims about charity, community, meaning, secular social outcomes, fertility, and inherited religious capital directly test which outlook can sustain flourishing institutions across generations.

sections.title: Equal rights, political secularism, and conscience
sections.rationale: The competing approaches to state neutrality, religious privilege, nondiscrimination, sexuality, and conscience exemptions bear directly on human rights and pluralistic freedom.

sections.title: Science, institutional autonomy, and intellectual progress
sections.rationale: The historical origins and institutional conditions of scientific inquiry matter to the debate's truth dimension and to each worldview's capacity to support continuing human advancement.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Christianity gradually helped generate Western commitments to human equality, human rights, abolition, and scientific method, and Jones argues that their stability is threatened by departure from their Christian foundation.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Secularization threatens community health because Christian missionary culture fostered democratic reform and research associates religious participation with sustained volunteering and charitable giving.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Jones argues that secularism produces low fertility and eventual cultural replacement, whereas Christianity can sustain population and preserve Western rights and pluralistic freedoms across generations.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: Christianity historically grounded protections for children and women, human rights, and limited government, while organized religious participation restrains authoritarian politics and supplies moral motivation.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: The realistic distribution of personal names in the Gospels and Acts is substantially more consistent with access to eyewitness information than with fictional composition.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-03.proposition: Suffering is compatible with Christianity if God's principal aim is forming virtuous souls through adversity and ultimately defeating evil rather than minimizing all present suffering.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-08.proposition: Christian human dignity supports equal civil rights and practical cooperation with humanists even amid disagreement over sexuality, religion, and lifestyle.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-10.proposition: Religious freedom can justify declining expressive participation in a same-sex wedding ceremony without permitting refusal of ordinary commercial service to gay customers.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-06.proposition: Jones argues that Islam subordinated foreign sciences to religious utility, whereas Christian institutional separation allowed science to develop autonomously and cumulatively.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-07.proposition: Christian belief in humanity's fallibility encouraged repeated experimentation and verification, thereby helping produce the scientific method and modern science.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: Political secularism requires a level playing field in which the state neither funds religious privilege nor gives clerics legislative power or believers unique exemptions from equal-rights rules.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Christianity's historical dominance does not establish unique causal credit for moral progress because Christians invoked the same framework both for and against reform, while some advances were led by nonreligious actors.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: A brighter future requires religiously neutral moral justification because grounding shared morality in declining Christianity excludes non-Christians and risks weakening common moral commitments.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: Healthy less-religious democracies and longstanding non-Christian moral traditions show that Christian belief is not necessary for decent, cooperative, and socially healthy societies.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: Christianity's truth requires God's existence, yet conceptions of a timeless person possessing temporally extended beliefs and desires face internal coherence problems.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Hundreds of millions of years of apparently unnecessary animal suffering constitute evidence against the existence of an all-powerful, perfectly loving, and perfectly good God.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: Christian immaterial-soul accounts conflict with ordinary physical causal closure and with neuroscientific findings that brain activity can predict choices before conscious decisions are reported.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-02.proposition: Cosmic fine-tuning may suggest some intelligence behind the universe, but it does not establish an all-powerful, supremely benevolent God, much less the specifically Christian God.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-07.proposition: The claim that successful secular societies merely consume inherited religious capital lacks supporting evidence and does not displace their observed present ability to function without religion.

chunk-003:chunk003-candidate-09.proposition: Humanists should resist special religious exemptions from generally applicable equal-rights protections because those exemptions can enable discrimination against women, racial minorities, and gay people.
